title: Two names for one key
summary: C♯ and D♭ are the same key. The natural sign means the plain white key.

steps.title: Enharmonic
steps.body:
Every black key now has two names. C♯ and D♭ are the same key and the same sound. Two names for the same key are called **enharmonic**.

**Why it matters:** Both names are correct and you will hear both. Which one a song uses depends on its key, which comes in Unit 3. For now, if someone says D♭ and you think C♯, you are right.

steps.title: Both names of each black key
White keys can have two names too
steps.body:
There is no black key between E and F, or between B and C. So E♯ is the same key as F, and C♭ is the same key as B.

**Why it matters:** you will not see these often, but now they will not surprise you when you do.

steps.title: The natural sign
steps.body:
The third accidental is the **natural** sign, ♮. It means the plain white key, with no sharp or flat. F♮ is just F.

**Why it matters:** You will see ♮ on charts when a note should be the plain white key rather than its sharp or flat neighbour.

items.prompt: Play Eb, the same key as D#.
Play Ab, the same key as G#.

steps.title: Hold a black key
steps.body: Press a black key and hold it. The app shows both of its names. Try all five black keys in one octave.

items.prompt: This key is C#. What is its other name?
